resources.string: Longshot captures the app window you choose and swipes it when you tap More. It uses scroll events and the positions of visible items to measure how far the page moved. Captures stay on this device.
Turn on Quick Tap. Tap the gear beside Open app, then the gear beside Longshot. Select Capture current page.
Double-tap the back of your phone to capture the current page.
Quick Tap opens Longshot’s home screen. Choose Capture current page using the gear beside Longshot.
Open Settings → System → Gestures → Quick Tap to start actions. Choose Open app, tap its gear, then use Longshot’s gear to choose Capture current page.
Open the controls on the page you want to save. Tap More to extend the image, or hold it to keep scrolling.
Accessibility is enabled. Capture controls will appear when Android connects Longshot.
To capture and scroll a page, select Longshot under Downloaded apps in Accessibility, turn on Use Longshot, then tap Allow.
Select Longshot in Accessibility, turn on Use Longshot, then tap Allow. Return here to continue to Quick Tap settings.

If Android blocks Longshot, tap the disabled Longshot entry in Accessibility once. In App info, open the three-dot menu and choose Allow restricted settings. Confirm with your screen lock if asked. Return to Longshot to finish enabling the service.
Long-press the Longshot icon and tap App info to open its settings.
Open Settings → Accessibility → Longshot. Turn on Use Longshot and tap Allow.
